name: switch
title: Switch
purpose: An on-or-off setting that takes effect as soon as it changes.
whenToUse: For a setting the app saves the moment it changes, such as Notify me when a run needs approval.
In a list of settings, one switch per row, each with its own label.
whenNotToUse: In a form that is sent with a button. Use a checkbox, which is read as part of the form.
To choose between two named options, such as Unified and Split. Use a segmented control.
To start or stop something that takes time or cannot be undone, such as cancelling a run. Use a button.
To show or hide part of the view from a toolbar. Use an icon button with aria-pressed.
accessibility: Use input type="checkbox" with role="switch" and ds-switch__input, and a label with ds-switch__label whose for attribute is the input's id. A screen reader announces the label, the switch role and on or off.
Inside the div with ds-switch the order is: the label, the state text, the input, then the description and the error if there are any.

The state text is a span with ds-switch__state and aria-hidden="true", holding two spans: ds-switch__on with the word On and ds-switch__off with the word Off. The stylesheet shows the one that matches the input, so no script changes the text. It is hidden from assistive technology because the switch role already says on or off. Always include it: with the thumb's position, it is what keeps the state from resting on colour.
The label names the setting and does not change with the state. Write it so that On means the thing in the label happens.
A description is a p with ds-switch__description, linked from the input with aria-describedby.

The component needs no script to move. The app listens for the change event and saves the setting. If saving fails, it sets the checked property back and adds a p with ds-switch__error and role="alert", linked through aria-describedby, saying which state the setting is in and what to do.
Set the disabled attribute when the setting cannot be changed, and say why in the description.

Tab reaches the switch and Space toggles it. The track is drawn 44px by 24px and its pointer target is as tall as the row, 40px by default and 44px on a coarse pointer; a press on the label toggles it too.
